label: H.R. 9645

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 25 - 15.

summary: H.R. 9645, titled the Health Care Price Certainty for All Americans Act, aims to promote health care price transparency and accountability across federal health programs, private health insurance, and group health plans. The bill requires hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging providers, and ambulatory surgical centers under Medicare to publicly disclose specific charges, rates, and cash prices. It updates price transparency and cost-sharing requirements for group health plans and health insurance issuers, protects pharmacies from restrictions on informing patients about prescription drug price differentials, and requires reporting on vertical integration in Medicare Advantage and prescription drug plans.

affected_groups.effect: Must publicly disclose standard charges, negotiated rates, and cash prices, submit annual compliance attestations, and face potential civil monetary penalties for noncompliance.
Must provide self-service cost-sharing tools for participants, publish quarterly rate and file information starting in 2029, and submit annual compliance attestations.
affected_groups.group: Group Health Plans and Health Insurance Issuers

affected_groups.effect: Allowed to inform patients of out-of-pocket cost differentials for prescription drugs without facing restrictions or penalties from plans or pharmacy benefit managers.
Required to submit periodic disclosures regarding provider and pharmacy ownership, financial risk arrangements, and incentive-based payments.
affected_groups.group: Medicare Advantage Organizations and PDP Sponsors

affected_groups.effect: Gains access to expanded price transparency data, self-service cost-sharing tools, plain language notices, and information regarding out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.

key_provisions: Requires specified hospitals, laboratories, imaging providers, and ambulatory surgical centers under Medicare to make standard charges, negotiated rates, and discounted cash prices publicly available and updated annually beginning in 2027 or 2028.
Establishes civil monetary penalties and compliance monitoring by the Secretary for health care facilities and providers that fail to comply with price transparency rules.

Updates group health plan and health insurance issuer requirements starting in 2029 to provide cost-sharing information through self-service tools and publish quarterly rate and payment data in machine-readable files.
Prohibits group health plans and pharmacy benefit managers from restricting or penalizing pharmacies from informing enrollees about out-of-pocket cost differentials compared to cash prices.
Requires large Medicare Advantage organizations and prescription drug plan sponsors to report health care provider and pharmacy ownership and financial risk arrangements starting in plan year 2028.
Appropriates $100 million total across fiscal years 2027 to 2032 to the Departments of Health and Human Services, the Treasury, and Labor for implementation and enforcement.
